title: U.S. Senate (special) · Ohio

context.text: This is a special election to fill the remainder of the U.S. Senate term won by J.D. Vance in 2022. Gov. Mike DeWine appointed Jon Husted to the seat on January 17, 2025 after Vance became vice president. The winner serves the rest of the term, through January 2029.
Sherrod Brown defeated Ron Kincaid in the Democratic primary on May 5, 2026, 89.4% to 10.6%. Jon Husted was unopposed in the Republican primary. Bill Redpath was unopposed in the Libertarian primary.

candidates.name: Jon Husted
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 5, 2026 Republican primary unopposed

summary.text: Husted is the incumbent Republican, appointed to the U.S. Senate by Gov. Mike DeWine in January 2025 to fill the seat vacated by J.D. Vance. A native of northwest Ohio and a University of Dayton graduate, he worked in Dayton-area government and the local chamber of commerce before serving in the Ohio House (2001-2009, Speaker 2005-2009), the Ohio Senate, as secretary of state (2011-2019) and as lieutenant governor (2019-2025). His campaign emphasizes his record in state office.

background.text: Born in Royal Oak, Michigan, in 1967. According to his Senate office biography, he began life in a foster home before being adopted by Jim and Judy Husted, and was raised in Williams County in northwest Ohio.

Graduated from Montpelier High School and earned a bachelor's degree in education (1989) and a master's degree in communications (1993) from the University of Dayton, where he played football; his Senate bio describes him as an All-American defensive back on the 1989 Division III national championship team.

Worked as a commission assistant to Montgomery County Commissioner Don Lucas (1993-1997) and as a color commentator on University of Dayton football broadcasts. In 1997 he joined the Dayton Area Chamber of Commerce, where he was director and vice president (his Senate bio lists the title Vice President for Economic Development).

Elected to the Ohio House of Representatives in 2000 and served from 2001 to 2009, including as Speaker from 2005 to 2009. According to his Senate office, as Speaker he led passage of a budget that included an income tax cut and created the EdChoice Scholarship.

Served in the Ohio Senate from 2009 to 2011, then as Ohio Secretary of State from 2011 to 2019. He was the named defendant in Husted v. A. Philip Randolph Institute (2018), in which the U.S. Supreme Court ruled in favor of Ohio's voter-roll maintenance process.

Served as lieutenant governor under Gov. Mike DeWine from 2019 to 2025, also directing the Governor's Office of Workforce Transformation. His Senate bio credits him with launching the TechCred job-training program and InnovateOhio.

Appointed to the U.S. Senate by Gov. DeWine on January 17, 2025, to replace Vice President J.D. Vance. In the 119th Congress he serves on the Committees on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions; Small Business and Entrepreneurship; Environment and Public Works; and Appropriations.
According to his Senate office, he and his wife, Tina, raised three children and live in Columbus, where they attend Riverside Church.

priorities.text: Campaigned on his record in state government, citing a 'conservative, balanced budget with the largest tax cut in Ohio history' as House speaker and economic development efforts as lieutenant governor.

record.text: Appointed by Gov. Mike DeWine to the U.S. Senate on January 17, 2025, to fill the seat vacated by J.D. Vance.
Serves on the Senate Special Committee on Aging, Committee on Environment and Public Works, Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions, and Committee on Small Business and Entrepreneurship.
As Ohio House speaker (2005-2009), signed off on a state budget he describes as including 'the largest tax cut in Ohio history.'

candidates.name: Sherrod Brown
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary, 89.4% to 10.6%

summary.text: Brown is the Democratic nominee and a former three-term U.S. senator from Ohio (2007-2025) who lost re-election to Bernie Moreno in 2024. A native of Mansfield, he began in the Ohio House at age 22, then served as secretary of state (1983-1991) and in the U.S. House (1993-2007) before winning the Senate seat in 2006. He is running to win back a seat for Democrats in the 2026 special election.

background.text: Born November 9, 1952, in Mansfield, Ohio, the son of Emily and Dr. Charles Gailey Brown.
Earned a bachelor's degree in Russian studies from Yale University in 1974, and later earned master's degrees in education and in public administration from Ohio State University.
Taught at Ohio State University's Mansfield campus from 1979 to 1981.
Elected to the Ohio House of Representatives while still in college and served as a state representative from 1975 to 1982; at his election, he was the youngest person elected to that body.
Elected Ohio Secretary of State in 1982 and re-elected in 1986, serving from 1983 to 1991; he lost a 1990 re-election bid to Republican Bob Taft.
Won the open seat for Ohio's 13th Congressional District in 1992 and served in the U.S. House from 1993 to 2007.

Elected to the U.S. Senate in 2006, defeating incumbent Mike DeWine, and re-elected in 2012 and 2018. He was the ranking Democrat on the Banking Committee from 2015 and chaired the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs from 2021 to 2025; he also served on the Finance, Agriculture, and Veterans' Affairs committees.

Lost re-election to Bernie Moreno in 2024, 50.1% to 46.5%. After leaving office he was a Spring 2025 visiting fellow at the Harvard Kennedy School and launched the Dignity of Work Institute, and on August 18, 2025, announced his candidacy for the 2026 special election.

priorities.text: Campaign website states he 'led the charge to make sure over 100,000 Ohioans got the retirement they were owed' and 'successfully fought to cap the cost of insulin and reduce the price of other prescription drugs for Ohio seniors.'
priorities.quote: led the charge to make sure over 100,000 Ohioans got the retirement they were owed

candidates.name: Bill Redpath
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 5, 2026 Libertarian primary unopposed

summary.text: Redpath is the Libertarian Party candidate. A Findlay, Ohio, native and retired business-valuation consultant now living in Perrysburg, he describes himself as a nine-time Libertarian candidate for public office and chaired the Libertarian National Committee from 2006 to 2010. His campaign focuses on reducing federal spending, repealing tariffs, and a non-interventionist foreign policy.

background.text: Born and raised in Findlay, Ohio; graduated from Findlay High School. As a teenager he worked at Findlay radio stations WFIN and WHMQ.
Earned a BA in economics and political science from Indiana University Bloomington (1978) and an MBA from the University of Chicago (1980).
Early finance and accounting career: auditor at Arthur Andersen in Cincinnati (1980-1982), WISH-TV in Indianapolis (1982-1983), ABC (1983-1984) and NBC (1984-1985) in New York.

Spent a 38-year career in business valuation focused on media and telecommunications, as vice president at BIA Advisory Services (1985-2020) and later managing director at Summit Ridge Group. He holds CPA, CFA (retired) and Accredited Senior Appraiser (retired) credentials.

Joined the Libertarian Party in 1984; served on the Libertarian National Committee for 24 years in total, including as chair from 2006 to 2010, and has led the party's ballot-access efforts. Says he was inducted into the Libertarian Party Hall of Liberty in 2016.

Has run for office repeatedly as a Libertarian: Virginia governor (2001), U.S. Senate (2008) and U.S. House (2010, 2014) in Virginia, and in Illinois for U.S. House (2020) and U.S. Senate (2022). He was Treasurer of the election-reform group FairVote (1995-2020).

priorities.text: Supports reducing federal spending, warning of a possible debt crisis, and wants the Federal Reserve to focus solely on an inflation target rather than a 'dual mandate' that also targets employment.
Calls for repealing all tariffs, including those imposed under the Trump administration, in favor of 'unilateral free trade.'
priorities.quote: Repeal not just Trump's tariffs, but all tariffs. I support a policy of unilateral free trade, which is a pro-consumer trade policy.

priorities.text: Supports open immigration except for criminals, terrorists, and others who would pose a danger, and opposes U.S. military interventionism.

positions.summary: Wants to repeal all tariffs, including those imposed under the Trump administration, favoring unilateral free trade.
positions.quote: Repeal not just Trump's tariffs, but all tariffs. I support a policy of unilateral free trade, which is a pro-consumer trade policy.

positions.summary: Supports open immigration, opposing broad enforcement/deportation, with exceptions only for criminals, terrorists, and those who would harm others.
positions.quote: All immigration should be allowed except for a handful of people who fall into the categories of criminals, terrorists, the seriously ill, or others who would harm the life, liberty, and property of people here.

positions.summary: Opposes the U.S. 'special relationship' with Israel's government, saying Israel should be treated like any other allied nation.
positions.quote: The "special relationship" with the government of Israel only leads the US into problems. We should treat Israel like any other allied nation.

candidates.name: Gregory Levy

summary.text: Gregory (Greg) Levy is an independent candidate for U.S. Senate who, according to his campaign website, is a community organizer, singer, veteran and mover from Akron, Ohio. His campaign describes itself as a socialist campaign, and its materials link it to the Party for Socialism and Liberation.

background.text: According to his campaign website, he was born in the Joy Park housing projects and raised in Akron, Ohio, the third of six boys; his father was a union electrician at Ford and his mother a nurse.
According to his campaign, he joined the military as a young man hoping to secure college funding, and his son was born during his service.
Works as a mover, according to his campaign, and founded the Paul Robeson Revolutionary Choir, which performs at church and community venues.
Qualified for the November 3, 2026, special general election ballot as an independent; no prior public office was found.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website, biography, or public policy statements found for Gregory Levy beyond Ballotpedia's fundraising figures. Could not confirm additional background.

researchNotes: Federal key votes and FEC totals for Husted and Brown are added separately by script. Husted's positions are drawn only from campaign messaging on his record and priorities rather than explicit statements matching the fixed issue list, so no `positions` entries were added for him; see `priorities` and `record` instead. Sherrod Brown's and Bill Redpath's own campaign/Candidate Connection material supplied clearer stance statements. Biography gaps: Gregory Levy's campaign website gives no birth year, education, or dates of military service; Sherrod Brown has no active official bio page, so his biography draws on Ballotpedia and Wikipedia.
